output.title: When a rollback drill is worth the time
output.body:
A rollback drill is worth doing when the change is hard to reverse and the workflow matters enough that a bad day would cost more than an hour of preparation.

For a small business owner, the question is simple: if this automation breaks, can I put the previous process back quickly, or will I be stuck untangling it while orders, invoices, or customer data sit in limbo?

That is the real cost of the drill. Not the exercise itself, but the time it takes to make reversal possible before something fails.

If money movement is involved, human approval still stays in the loop. That part should not be automated away just because the rest of the workflow is.

The practical next step is boring on purpose: before the next change, write down the current manual fallback or the single point of failure, then run a small rollback drill and see how long it takes to return to the prior state. If you cannot say that out loud with confidence, the drill is probably worth the time.

Unglamorous, yes. Useful, also yes.
